description:
Tier 1. Anchors: blake2_elixir / blake2 (Rustler over the blake2 crate), b3 (Rustler over the blake3 crate). BLAKE2b (RFC 7693) is 12 rounds of a u64 G function over a 16-word state; the reference is plain C and is the expectation for parity. BLAKE3's reference has SIMD (AVX2/NEON) and a tree mode; its portable C (blake3_portable.c) is the fair comparison, and the verdict against the SIMD build is expected poor and reported as such.

Kernels: `blake2b(msg :: [u8], outlen :: i64) :: [u8]` with keyed variant optional; `blake3(msg :: [u8]) :: [u8]` single-threaded with the chunk/parent tree computed iteratively over an alloc'd stack of chaining values (no recursion in the subset). Constants (IV, sigma permutations) as module attributes.

Elixir baseline: a pure Elixir BLAKE2b (check Hex; if none, a straightforward Elixir implementation with bitwise BIFs marked :first_pass, then optimised). :crypto has blake2b/blake2s since OTP 22 (if OpenSSL has them): report it beside as the ceiling.

Realistic size: 1 KB to 64 MB (content hashing, dedup); measure 64 KB and 64 MB.

Expected verdict: good vs pure Elixir; marginal vs :crypto's blake2b; poor vs b3's SIMD, parity with blake3_portable.

Needs: defk-w38, defk-n4r.2 (u64 and u32 loads, wrapping add, rotates), defk-ivt, defk-n4r.4 (the compression function as a helper writing the state array).

Done when: RFC 7693 and BLAKE3 official vectors pass, agreement holds, verdicts measured, README row added.

comments.text:
Done in 348541d (branch defk-52v.2/blake2b-blake3, not merged). examples/blake.exs, three DEFK_RESULT lines. All numbers provisional (load 13-135 on 12 cores).

Verdicts (pre-registered expectations all held):
- blake (BLAKE2b-512, 64 KB): good, 31.8-32.7x over the optimised Elixir (1.37-1.43 ms vs 0.042-0.049 ms); 64 MB 32.5-33.3x; 1 KB 21-22x. blake2_elixir (reference C NIF) 1.02x: parity.
- blake_crypto: marginal, 1.16-1.19x over :crypto.hash(:blake2b) (1.0x at 1 KB). Use :crypto.
- blake3 (64 KB): good, 10.6-10.9x over the optimised Elixir; 64 MB 10.1x. Level with BLAKE3 portable C measured outside the BEAM (52 us / 55 ms vs kernel 54-59 us / 55-60 ms); 0.6x of the blake3 NIF (NEON). Tick gaps at 64 MB: NIFs block 34-49 ms, kernels 2.1-2.7 ms.

Correction to the ticket: b3 0.2.1 is pure Elixir (already tuned), not Rustler; the Rust NIF is blake3 1.0.2 (needs rustler 0.30 pinned). blake2 1.0.4 is pure Elixir, blake2_elixir 0.9.0 is the C NIF; the two clash on Blake2/Blake2.Mixfile, so blake2 is fetched with compile: false and compiled as HexBlake2.

Elixir tried (BLAKE2b, 64 KB): blake2 package 31-67 ms, 64-bit words unrolled 14.4 ms (first pass), 32-bit halves unrolled 1.37-1.43 ms (baseline). BLAKE3: b3 0.60-0.63 ms, struct-free rewrite 0.56-0.58 ms (baseline). Not tried: parallel BLAKE3 subtrees (same trick on both sides), lazy masking in halves.

Kernel: SIGMA round loop from a binary attribute 48-49 us vs unrolled 43 us. BLAKE3 masked rotate 79-80 us; rotr(x,n,32) 95-98 us before, 54-55 us after a tiny runtime fix in this ticket (defk_rot_w rotates w=32 as uint32_t -> one ror; test added in u64_test). No language gaps found: tuple-returning helper kernels, ctz for the merge count, array in a tuple accumulator all worked. Still kept: 16 bounds checks per block on u32_le/u64_le from a helper's src/off (not costly here).

Docs: examples/README rows (helps table + blake_crypto in Elixir table), performance.md 2.14, 3.9, 6.14, 7.5.

title: BLAKE2b and BLAKE3 from scratch vs blake2_elixir and b3 NIFs
